# Loaders: patcher download, Steam re-patch, bookmarklet notice

## Source and generated files

- `src/loader/shared/` holds the implementation. `scanner.mjs` walks delimiters, `patch-finders.mjs` locates anchors, `patch-bundle.mjs` applies the rules, and `browser-loader.mjs` starts the game and mod in the browser. The scanner recognises regex literals in common expression and control-header positions, division, comments and nested template expressions. Function-header finders still target the shapes emitted by the game minifier.
- `userscript-entry.mjs` holds the shared bridge and bootstrap code for Live and local Dev. The generated scripts keep their own install URLs and metadata, including the editable `repo` and `version` in the bridge. Steam uses the same `patchBundle` through `patcher-entry.cjs` and injects the mod through its preload.
- Run `npm run build:loaders` after editing source. It writes the four standalone scripts in `src/loader/` and `synergism_modloader/lib/patcher.js`. Keep those files with the source change. Older Steam loaders call the patcher as a function and browsers read its `startBrowserLoader` property from the downloaded file. `npm test` checks that the files match the source. The dev server generates its own copies in `build/`.

## When each loader picks up patcher.js and the mod

- Browser: at each page load. The userscript takes it from jsDelivr (`master` of `window.__HS_REPO`, `Ferlieloi` by default).
- Steam: only when the player patches ("Patch & launch"). The loader takes it from the selected channel's repo and ref (`lib/config.js`, `buildPatcherUrl` in `main.js`), and falls back to its bundled copy only when the download fails or takes more than 15 s. The patcher's own messages go to the loader's console (`runPatcher` in `lib/patchGame.js` passes it `log` and `warn`): a `[PATCH] WARNING:` line is a patch step that could not be applied, shown in orange and counted at the end of the patch. `local/game/out.js` is the browser bundle, so the "Steam auto-sync" step always warns on it. "Launch only", "Launch last played build" and "Quick switch" reuse the game as last patched and only change the mod URL (`HS_MOD_URL`).
- Steam, when a re-patch is asked: when the game exe changed (size or date), and when the selected build's patcher is not the one the game was patched with (`lib/patcherSource.js`, `patcher:check-changed` in `main.js`). The patch stores a hash of the patcher it used (`lastPatchedPatcherHash`); the check downloads the build's `patcher.js` (5 s limit) and compares. A build without `patcher.js` (404) is compared with the bundled copy, as a patch of it would use that. No stored hash (game patched by a loader up to 0.2.8) asks for one re-patch. A failed download asks for nothing (a console line says so). Three more cases, all checked without a download: the injector written into the game is not the one this loader writes (`lastPatchedInjectorHash` against `injectorHash()` in `lib/injectorTemplate.js`; the hash leaves the mod URL out), the patched copy is missing (`game:check-update-needed` answers `reason: 'missing'`), and the copy was built another way (`lastPatchedFormat` against `PATCH_FORMAT` in `lib/patchGame.js`, `reason: 'format'`; raise the number when a loader change needs the game patched again; no number = a loader up to 0.2.9). On step 3: a banner, "Launch only" and "Quick switch" disabled, and the Quick switch banner hidden. On step 1: "Launch last played" becomes "Patch & launch last played" and patches first (for a game update too, which that button ignored before). The check follows what jsDelivr serves, so on a branch it can lag a push by up to 12 hours unless the file was purged. Loaders up to 0.2.8 only ask when the game was updated: their players can run a new mod on a game patched by an older patcher until they patch again.
- Steam, the mod itself: the game downloads it at each launch from the URL the loader passes in `HS_MOD_URL`, and keeps it in its browser cache (`%APPDATA%/synergismofficial/Cache`). jsDelivr sends a 7-day `max-age` on a branch (`@master`), and a jsDelivr purge doesn't reach that cache. So `buildModUrl` (`lib/patchGame.js`) adds `?t=<timestamp>` to every mod URL, as the browser loader does. Loaders up to v0.2.7 don't: their players on `master` can keep an old mod for up to 7 days after a release (a tag is a new URL, so it is never stale).
- Steam, the extraction: the loader ships its own `7za.exe` (`7zip-bin`, copied to `resources/7zip-bin/` by `extraResources`), so players need no 7-Zip. `7za` has no NSIS module, but finds `app-64.7z`, stored uncompressed in the game's installer, and extracts the app in one step; a full `7z.exe` (a player's saved path) still goes through `$PLUGINSDIR/app-64.7z`. `patchGame` extracts the exe into `exe/` and handles both. Not the full 7-Zip from a git-ignored `vendor/`: CI can't bundle it.
- Steam, the repack: the game keeps its native modules (`steamworks-ffi-node` and `koffi`, 213 files; `steamworks.js` before game build 26392693) outside `app.asar`, in `app.asar.unpacked`, and `steam_api64.dll` in `resources/steamworks_sdk/`. The patch reads those directories from the original archive's header (`readUnpackedDirs` in `lib/archiveWriter.js`) and repacks with the same ones outside. Packed inside (loaders up to 0.2.9), the `.node` is loaded from a copy in `%TEMP%`, away from `steam_api64.dll`: the game still started from the loader (the working folder has that dll), but the login's return (`synergism://` link, a second instance started by Windows from another folder) crashed. `@electron/asar` keeps each archive's file list by path and the staging path is fixed, so the patch calls `asar.uncache` before reading it.
- Checking what a patch applied: `window.__HS_PATCH_REPORT` (both loaders, see below). What it exposed: `__HS_BACKDOOR__.exposed` exists only in the browser loader (`startBrowserLoader` in `patcher.js`); the Steam injector has no equivalent, so on Steam read the `window.__HS_*` globals directly in the console. Old and new patcher code can print the same `[PATCH]` line: to know which one patched the Steam game, look for its injected text in `dist/dist/out.js` of `__hs_work_current/app/resources/app.asar`.

## Browser: the game's second address (pseudo-corp.github.io)

The game is also served at `https://pseudo-corp.github.io/SynergismOfficial/` (GitHub Pages, rebuilt by the game's `deploy-ghpages.yml` at every push to its `master`, so it can be ahead of synergism.cc). Asked for by a player whose work network blocks synergism.cc. There the game turns login, cloud saves and purchases off (`isSynergismCC` in `Config.ts`), and its saves are that site's own `localStorage`, apart from synergism.cc's. The 4 userscripts `@match` it too (bridge 1.3, loader 4.2: Tampermonkey updates an installed bridge through its `@updateURL`). The browser loader downloads the bundle from the page's own copy (`gameBundleUrl` in `patcher.js`: `https://synergism.cc/dist/out.js` on synergism.cc, else `dist/out.js` against `document.baseURI`). Before that, it always downloaded synergism.cc's bundle: blocked there, the loader stopped after blocking the page's own script, so the game never started. synergism.cc answers `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, so where it isn't blocked the old code ran synergism.cc's bundle in github.io's HTML. The mod itself needs nothing: its requests to synergism.cc (`stripe/upgrades`, `users/me`) fail into a log line, as the game's own do (synergism.cc's CORS only allows `https://synergism.cc`, so they never succeed from github.io), and translations are fetched relative to the page first. Skipping those two requests off synergism.cc (2 red Log lines at each load) was dropped. Tested headless on the real github.io with synergism.cc blocked (13/13 patches, mod loaded; Live's old patcher: "Failed to fetch"); `scripts/harness/loader-https.cjs` (the patcher is served by answering the jsDelivr request through CDP `Fetch`, since an https page can't reach `http://127.0.0.1`).

## Browser: the game started before the loader

Sometimes Tampermonkey runs the userscript late (its own content script fetches the script by message instead of injecting it at document-start, e.g. when its worker was asleep), and the original game (`<script defer>`, fast from the cache) registers `tab-row`/`sub-tab` first. The guard (`guardBrowserGameElements`) then throws an error flagged `hsGameStartedFirst`, at the loader's start or just before injection. The download of `patcher.js` can't cause it: the userscripts fetch it with synchronous XHRs, which block the page. `startBrowserLoader`'s `fail` then shows a banner at the top of the page ("the game started before the mod's loader. Reloading… (n/3)") and reloads 1.5 s later, up to 3 times in a row. They're counted in `sessionStorage` (`hs-loader-late-start-reloads`, forgotten after 60 s, cleared once a patched bundle runs). After that, a closable banner says to refresh, plus the "Allow User Scripts" hint outside Firefox. It reloads nothing more, and a manual refresh gets its 3 reloads again. Without `sessionStorage`, it never reloads (nothing would stop a loop). Other loader errors are unchanged: a console warning only. The mod's setting `reloadOnLateLoaderStart` ("Reload when the loader starts late", UI page, on by default, shown to userscript players only) turns the reload off: the loader reads it from `localStorage` (`hs-settings`) like `autoDismissOfflinePopup`, and when it's off, the closable banner shows right away.

## How patchBundle finds and reports its patches

- **Writing a patch.** Anchor it on what the code does: string literals (translation keys, ids like `"Exalt9x1"`) and
  property names that minification keeps (`lifetimeAmbrosia`, `cubeUpgrades[29]`), through the finders below, never a
  call-site shape or a minified name: the game updates often and players get the patcher at each launch, so a brittle
  anchor breaks for everyone at once. Give the finder the patch's label (it warns when several places match), set the
  patch's `report` entry, put top-of-bundle lines in `topLines`. Check on the browser bundle and the Steam one that the
  summary says "N/N applied" with no "to check", and look at which function each patch logs: a unique-looking anchor
  can still land in the wrong function. Cover `$`-prefixed names and other shapes in a loader test.

- **Finders, by what the code does.** `findEnclosingFunction(code, anchorRe, markers, label)`: around each match of the anchor, the nearest named function holding every marker. `findAssignedObjectLiteral(code, keyRe, markers, label)`: the object literal assigned to a variable (`x={…}`) with that key at its own level, wherever it sits (player, consumables). The dialog hook finds each queued action (`.enqueue(()=>{` with `confirmationBox`) and tells them apart by the one wrapper id the action doesn't hide (each dialog hides the 4 others). Steam auto-sync only looks inside saveSynergy (`"testing.gameSaved"`) and wants exactly one throttle test there. Parameter lists accept one level of parentheses in defaults (`PARAMS`).
- **Ambiguity warning.** When an anchor and its markers match more than one function (or literal), the first is still patched and a `[PATCH] WARNING:` line names the others ("N places match its anchor — patched X, also Y"). The tack patch landed in addTimers that way: such a warning after a game update means the anchor needs another marker. On Steam it is counted with the steps not applied. The labels of those patches go into the bundle as `window.__HS_PATCH_AMBIGUOUS` (an array), and the summary line ends with "to check (several matches): …".
- **Report.** Each patch sets its entry in `report`; the bundle gets `window.__HS_PATCH_REPORT = { export, exportOutput, stage, player, getMaxChallenges, corruptionFreeLevels, tack, dialogHook, validateBlueberryTree, saveImportHook, consumables, globalEvent, saveSeedCap, steamAutoSync (Steam only) }` (true = applied; the mod leaves the retired `applyCorruptions`, still in the report of installs patched before game 4.4.0, out of its "patch incomplete" warning: `Hypersynergism.#RETIRED_PATCHES`), and the log ends with `Bundle patching complete: N/M applied — missing: …`.
- **A missing patch only costs what it adds.** The browser loader (`runPostLoadSequence`) reads the report: without the stage patch it doesn't open Misc or wait for the stage; without the export patch it never clicks `#exportgame` (it would run a real export and its rewards). A wait that times out (20 s) is a warning, and the mod loads anyway. The mod's `#ensurePatcherExposure` (Steam) skips the same steps, and `#reportPatchProblems` tells the player once at load when a patch is missing or in doubt (`__HS_PATCH_AMBIGUOUS`): a warning notification (10 s, top) and the detail in the Log tab. A patcher older than the report: both behave as if every patch applied.
- **Lines for the top of the bundle go through `topLines`**, written after the bundle's `"use strict"` directive. Before it, the directive becomes a plain string and the whole game runs in sloppy mode.

- **Manual ascension** (`manualAscension` in the report) wraps the confirmed reset in `resetConfirmation`. The mod uses this hook for the [Ascension loadout](ascension-loadout.md), including Shift+A. The game still runs its normal reset when the mod is absent.

## Bookmarklet notice

**Bookmarklet players are told to switch** (`HSBookmarkletNotice`, `hs-core/hs-bookmarklet-notice.ts`, static, not an `HSModule`). A bookmark load is: in a browser (not Steam) and `window.HS_LOADER_INITIALIZED` not set. Every userscript loader sets that flag before the game runs, so a userscript whose patch failed is not counted. At each such load, a mod modal (non-blocking, no "don't show again") gives the steps: Tampermonkey's page in the store of the player's browser (from the user agent), the "Allow User Scripts" step on Chrome-based browsers, an "Install the script" link to the bridge userscript on jsDelivr (a userscript manager opens its install page for a URL ending in `.user.js`), and a Copy button as the fallback. The copied text is `src/loader/tampermonkey-bridge.user.js` itself, inlined at build time, always Live (`Ferlieloi`, `master`). The same players get a section at the very top of the Tools tab that opens the modal again.

## Globals set late

Some patcher globals are also set late. The stage patch sets `__HS_i18next`, `__HS_synergismStage` and `DOMCacheGetOrSet` only once the game runs `loadMiscellaneousStats` (Settings → Stats for nerds → Misc).
- The browser loader's `runPostLoadSequence` opens that view before it loads the mod.
- The Steam injector (`injectorTemplate.js`) does not. Instead, the mod's `Hypersynergism.#ensurePatcherExposure()` does the same navigation plus a silent export once the game has loaded, whenever the bundle is patched but these globals are still missing. It runs behind the offline popup when that is open.
- Both the browser loader and the mod close the offline popup at load only when the `autoDismissOfflinePopup` setting is on. The loader reads it straight from `localStorage` (`hs-settings`), because the mod isn't loaded yet at that point.

## Testing the Steam loader

- **Commands**, from `synergism_modloader/` (its own npm package and version): `npm start` (Electron app), `npm test` (`node --test test/*.test.js`, also after a `patcher.js` change), `npm run dist` (installer).
- **Test fs code in Electron, not node.** Electron treats `.asar` paths as folders: it opens the archive and keeps it open. A `fs.existsSync(…/app.asar)` in `patchGame` passed in plain node and failed in the real loader (EPERM renaming the folder, EBUSY on `app.asar`). Any fs access to an asar path goes through `withRawArchiveAccess` (`process.noAsar`, `lib/patchGame.js`). After a change to `lib/patchGame.js`, `workspaceManager.js` or `archiveWriter.js`, run from `synergism_modloader/`: `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 ./node_modules/electron/dist/electron.exe test/packagedPatchSmoke.js <synergism_modloader folder, Windows path> "<Steam>/steamapps/common/Synergism/Synergism-win-x64.exe" <7z or 7za path>` (three patches on a temporary copy, about 2 minutes).
- **An Electron main script prints nothing when `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1` is set** in the environment (some shells set it): it runs as plain node, no window, no `app`. Run it with the variable removed (`env -u ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE …`). The loader has Electron 31; the Steam game ships Electron 39. A small game-like app (the same `protocol.handle('https')` + preload `fetch`, a temporary `userData`, `webRequest.onCompleted` giving `fromCache`) answers questions about the game's browser cache and network stack.
- **The re-patch check follows what jsDelivr serves, not git**: `@master` can serve an older `patcher.js` for hours after a push unless the file is purged.

## Checking the Steam bundle

`local/game/out.js` is the browser build: Steam-only code (`PLATFORM === 'steam'`, e.g. the cloud-sync throttle the "Steam auto-sync" patch targets) is compiled out. To get the Steam one:
1. `synergism_modloader/node_modules/7zip-bin/win/x64/7za.exe x "<Steam>/steamapps/common/Synergism/Synergism-win-x64.exe" -o<scratch>/steam/exe -y`. This `7za` unpacks straight to `resources/app.asar` (no `app-64.7z` step, unlike a full 7-Zip).
2. From `synergism_modloader/`: `require('@electron/asar').extractFile(asarPath, path.join('dist','dist','out.js'))`. Archive paths use backslashes: a `'dist/dist/out.js'` string is "not found".
3. Delete the ~400 MB extraction, keep only `out.js`.
4. Run the patcher with `steam: true`, as the loader does: `node scripts/tools/patcher-targets.cjs <out.js> steam`. Without `steam: true` the summary still looks complete, one patch short of the real count, and auto-sync is never checked. `steamapps/appmanifest_*.acf` says whether Steam has installed the latest build (`buildid` against `TargetBuildID`).

`__hs_work_current` in the game folder holds the last patched game, so it is stale after a game update: compare its date with the exe's.

## Decisions

- **One loader at a time** (`app.requestSingleInstanceLock`): a second start brings the first loader to the front and closes, with a line in the console and in `loader-startup.log`. The lock follows the user data folder, which the installed loader and `npm start` share: close one to run the other.
- **Re-patch banner:** "Launch last played" patches first when a re-patch is needed (a game update too); no stored hash asks for one re-patch; any patcher difference blocks "Launch only" and "Quick switch", switching builds included; a failed download asks for nothing (a console line). Downloading the patcher and the mod by commit id (`@<sha>`) to avoid jsDelivr's lag was refused.
- **Bookmarklet notice:** shown at every bookmark load, no "don't show again"; the script is always Live (`Ferlieloi`, `master`); only Tampermonkey is named; the README's bookmark loads from `Ferlieloi@master`.
